data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test describes its subject when the subject is the test's own installation condition; the 3-of-26 result is a description of the author's own care, not a constraint on the mutations, because the same author's ordinary guards already encoded the acceptance record's expectations.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If an independent author had written the mutations, the test's constraints would be measurable.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the mutations were generated without access to the acceptance record, the description hypothesis would be weakened.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 3 survivors were replicated across authors, the test would be constraining the code rather than the author.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The author wrote both the tests and the mutations in the same week, so the tests describe the author's intended invariants rather than constraining the mutations. The 3-of-26 survivors are mutations that the author's own guards did not anticipate, so the test's failure to catch them is a property of the author, not of the code.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
